verdict.why:
I wrote my own classifier from the shape tests as the summary words them and ran it over all 148,506 rows. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mashiachsonyosef-github-io/c72302ec-11e7-5b6d-a5ab-47bb077585fe/scratchpad/punct/verify/wikisource_strongs_explicit_forms/ (lib.mjs, verify.mjs, compare.mjs, falsify.mjs, falsify2.mjs, falsify3.mjs, falsify4.mjs, diag-paren.mjs, each with its .out.json). The locator puts every route in its definition. 11,023 routes occur more than once there; they are placed in order, preferring an item-bounded occurrence in the list.

WHAT REPRODUCES EXACTLY:
- Every mark's total occurrences and the number of routes carrying it, including X 11,910 and each of the 13 Hebrew points.
- The opener spellings.
- 41 of 54 shape counts: every comma shape (259 head-aside commas = 255 in the head + 4 in definitions with no opener), every semicolon, hyphen, '+', colon and single-shape count, and for '.' list_end 108, head_sentence_end 6 and stray 8.
- For '(': head_aside 174 (158 + 16 in no-opener definitions), note 77, suffix 9,589, opener_never_closed 120. For ')': closer_with_nothing_open 141.
- The declaration divides 431 routes into 982 pieces.
- The whole v3 comparison: 148,133 same / 8 / 121 / 15, with 229 withheld and 196 that divide the same but print differently. With damaged senses held whole: 148,361 / 8 / 122 / 15.

WHAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE (13 shape counts):
- '(' and ')', read as the tests are worded: optional_words 23,659 (draft 23,603), alternatives 9,420 (9,177), prefix_syllable 2,125 (2,526), list_aside 553 (527). 76 groups fit no shape: 72 are '(+)' and 4 are '((handy-, needle-, net-))'.
- The draft's numbers do come out exactly (diag-paren.mjs, variant D) once three rules are added that its census.mjs uses but the tests never state. The prefix test runs before alternatives and also takes contents ending '-)'. '(+)' counts as optional_words. The aside list is the code's regex, which leaves out '(from margin)' (33 groups) and adds 7 groups the test never names.
- X: whole_rendering 11,305 (draft 11,263), mid_rendering 62 (draft 104). The draft measured "first in the rendering" from the start of the route. That moves 42 X's that open a rendering after an opener in the middle of the route, or after a ';' in a definition with no opener, into mid_rendering. Examples: נרדה ');  -X abundantly', עד '; X and'.
- '.': abbreviation 127 (draft 126) and note_sentence_end 67 (draft 68). The difference is 'Prob.' at לחם.
- Ellipsis: 612 dots sit in a '...' run. The draft's 616 adds 4 dots from two-dot runs: גזל 'perverting.. gozal' and דא 'one..another'.

COMPLETENESS: under the tests as written, 152 paren occurrences fit no shape, and neither do the 4 two-dot periods. Several tests also overlap, and nothing states which one wins:
- optional_words also matches the suffix (6,815), prefix (2,125) and aside (553) groups.
- 230 groups match both alternatives and prefix.
- All 733 comma.in_unclosed_group commas also pass the in_group test.
- 210 hyphens match both opener_tail and suffix.
- The test "'(' with no ')' after it" literally fails for 113 of the 120 never-closed openers, because a ')' that closes an inner group follows them.

Under the draft code's own order, every occurrence does land in exactly one shape.

FALSIFICATION: I made at least 3 attempts on every dividing shape.
- No counterexamples: the opener shapes (5 attempts), the comma separator, and the stated counts for lone groups (177) and citation-colon cuts (45).
- Counterexamples that the declaration does not state with a count: period.list_end 12 + 2 routes, semicolon.head_separator 27, semicolon.rendering_separator 2 + 1. Details are in falsified_meanings.

So holds is false.
falsified_meanings: period.list_end, stated meaning 'ends the rendering list; what follows is a note or cross-reference stub': in 12 routes across 3 definitions the piece after the stop is a KJV rendering, a full stop written where a comma belongs. These are גבולת 'landmark. place' and מלין 'thing. word' (10 routes in those 2 definitions) and לודיים/לודים 'Ludim. Lydians' (2 routes). The declaration names 'Ludim. Lydians' and 'landmark. place' but gives no count and leaves out 'thing. word'. In 2 more routes the piece after the stop is transcription debris, not a note: יצרים 'member.ql' and יעף '-swiftly.e'. Counted by falsify2.mjs.

semicolon.head_separator, stated meaning 'separates etymology from sense and one sense from the next': in 27 occurrences (14 routes, 4 definitions) one side is a variant spelling of the headword, which is neither etymology nor sense. Examples: פדיון 'or pidyom; also pidyown; or pidyon', מצדה 'or (feminine) mtsuwdah; or mtsudah', נצח 'or netsach; from', סלון 'or callown; from'. The declaration states no such exception. Softer finding: in 10 occurrences in 6 definitions with no opener, the right side is the KJV rendering list itself, so the ';' is doing the opener's job. Examples: דתי 'corresponding to דָּת; decree', עד 'corresponding to עַד; X and'.

semicolon.rendering_separator, stated meaning 'separates one KJV rendering from the next': in 2 routes, ירע and ירעה '4; the rest belong to רָעַע)', the ';' sits inside the provider's aside '(only Isa. 15:4; the rest belong to ...)'. The store cut the group's '(' off at the citation colon. The declaration still cuts the aside, because the stray ')' is treated as inert and so '( )' does not protect it; falsify4.mjs finds these 2 are the only cuts anywhere inside a group the definition opened. In 1 more route, חראי 'excrement; -dung', the ';' together with its '-' is the provider's '; -' opener, displaced after a colon. 'excrement' is Strong's definition, not a KJV rendering, yet the declaration calls it 'the first rendering'.

comma.rendering_separator: there is only 1 occurrence in route text (אחרחל '--Aharhel,', a trailing comma), and its meaning holds. But the stated exception of '67 syllable-led routes' counts 64 by my script: 21 led by a hyphen and 43 led by '(-'. Lone groups (177) and citation-colon cuts (45) reproduce. 137 list routes that are a bare function word ('ד: but', 'עמ: and') are genuine KJV renderings of particles, so that attempt failed to falsify.

Shapes that do not divide, recorded but not counted against holds: paren.optional_words ('a word sometimes given with the principal word') is wrong for the 33 '(from margin)' groups (מעבדים) and for the 72 '(+)' groups (יריתי), which hold no word. paren.prefix_syllable ('a syllable added to the start of the following word') is only partly right for the 243 comma groups the code files there, such as חלק '(have, im-)' and יעמד '(make to, ..., with-)'. period.stray_in_rendering includes בג '(from the margin for baz.)', which is a sentence end inside an aside.
corrections: Paren tests: state the rules census.mjs actually applies, or recount from the tests as worded. To get 23,603 / 9,177 / 2,526 / 527, prefix_syllable must be tested before alternatives and must accept contents that end '-' or '-)'. That moves 243 comma groups such as '(have, im-)' and 154 nested groups such as '((wash-))' into prefix. Also state that '(+)' counts as optional_words.

paren.list_aside: put '(from margin)' among the asides. It is the same note as 'from the margin', and it is the 33 groups the code leaves in optional_words: list_aside goes up by 33 and optional_words down by 33. Write out the full phrase list instead of 'and the like', including the 7 the code adds: '(with the article)', '(often used as a part of proper names)', '(figuratively)'.
'(+)' (72 groups) holds a sign, not a word. Either give it its own shape (an optional '+' sign) or reword the optional_words test and meaning to cover it.
paren.opener_never_closed test: reword to "'(' that no ')' in the route closes". Literally, 'no ')' after it' is false for 113 of the 120.
paren.head_aside and comma.in_head_aside: add '(or a definition with no opener)', as the semicolon test already says. 16 groups and 4 commas sit in definitions with no opener.

State the test order wherever tests overlap: aside, then suffix, then prefix, then alternatives, then optional for '('; in_unclosed_group before in_group for ',' (all 733 also pass in_group); opener_tail and misplaced_opener_tail before suffix_syllable for '-' (210 and 1 overlaps).

X: as worded ('first in the rendering, after any opener tail') the counts are whole_rendering 11,305 and mid_rendering 62. Either correct the counts, or reword the test to measure from the start of the route, which reproduces 11,263 / 104 and leaves the 42 X's that open a rendering after a mid-route opener, such as נרדה '-X abundantly', labeled mid_rendering.

'.': 'Prob.' (לחם) is an abbreviation, so abbreviation is 127 and note_sentence_end 67. Reword ellipsis to 'part of a run of two or more dots' to cover the 4 dots in 'perverting.. gozal' and 'one..another'; otherwise those 4 fit no shape.

period.list_end: add a counted exception of 12 routes in 3 definitions where the piece after the stop is a KJV rendering ('landmark. place', 'thing. word', 'Ludim. Lydians'), plus 2 routes where it is transcription debris ('member.ql', '-swiftly.e'). Under open question 1's Reading B, those 12 renderings would be printed as notes.
semicolon.head_separator: extend the meaning to 'or separates variant spellings of the headword' and count it: 27 occurrences, 14 routes, 4 definitions (פדיון, מצדה, נצח, סלון).

semicolon.rendering_separator: when the route holds a ')' with nothing open, treat the text before it as inside a group and do not cut there (or take depth from the definition). Otherwise the declaration cuts the provider's aside at ירע/ירעה (2 routes). Also note חראי: there ';' plus '-' is the displaced '; -' opener, so 'excrement' is the definition, not a rendering.
Fix the stated exception for comma.rendering_separator: there are 64 syllable-led list routes (21 led by '-', 43 led by '(-'), not 67.
Make the summary agree with itself: hyphen.opener_tail and hyphen.misplaced_opener_tail are marked divides:false, but the declaration's separates_on lists both in the opener cut.

questions: 1. Head and note pieces in a divided route. 431 routes divide into 982 pieces. 434 pieces are KJV renderings. 440 come from Strong's own definition (220 shaped like an etymology: 'a primitive root', 'from ...', '(Aramaic) corresponding to ...'). 108 are notes after the list ('Yrechow', '(Superlative of ...)', 'ql'). Together they sit in 330 routes. Reading A: each piece prints as a reading, which is what today's engine already does with head pieces it cuts at ';'. Reading B: each piece is kept but printed as the provider's definition or note beside the readings, not as a reading. Some 'notes' are really a full stop written where a comma belongs ('Ludim. Lydians'; 'landmark. place' in 6 routes); those are renderings under either reading.

2. Damaged parentheses: 229 routes print nothing today because gloss-store with sense-split rule 4 holds back a damaged sense. They print whole under the August refusal rules, which this declaration keeps (closer with nothing open: inert, 141 routes; opener never closed: separate up to it, 93 routes). Reading A: print whole. Reading B: withhold. Of the 229, 187 come from a definition whose own parentheses don't balance and 42 from a store cut through a group the provider closed. For those 42 only, a third course is to have the store re-cut at the provider's group.

3. Notation with no principal word: 201 list routes are a syllable or a group standing alone. 67 lead with a suffix ('-s', '-th', '-or)', '(-ing father)'). 177 are one group with nothing outside it ('(put)', '(deal, make)', '(depart)'). The two sets overlap. The store cut them at the provider's depth-0 comma. Reading A: print them as they stand. Reading B: the store re-cuts so each stays with the rendering the provider attached it to ('seven(-fold),-s', in 20 definition rows). That is a store change, not a join made on the page.

4. What '+' means (4,743 occurrences in 4,733 routes). August says 'supplied by the translators and not in the Hebrew'. This declaration uses Strong's own sign: a rendering made together with one or more other Hebrew words. The division is the same either way; only the gloss on the sign changes. The store doesn't carry Strong's 'signs employed' page, so the owner confirms.
5. '&' in the rendering list (18 routes: '& presume', 'lay & to (take a) pledge'). Reading A: it means 'and'. Reading B: it is an X or + damaged in transcription. Nothing divides either way.

6. License: August's export line names cc_by_4_0_underlying_public_domain. The store's M14 record today says cc_by_sa_4_0_underlying_public_domain (share-alike). The declaration follows the store, and this governs the export of all 148,506 routes.

7. Routes cut after a chapter:verse colon (45 routes, such as the bare verse numbers '3' x8, '11' x10, '18' x2, '10' x1, and '48 marg)'). Today's engine prints 30 and withholds 15; this declaration prints all 45 whole. Reading A: print them as the provider's characters. Reading B: the store re-cuts the definition, reading the citation colon as a citation.
